newsitem.title: FRANCE: Four bomb attacks hit Corsica, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Four bomb attacks hit Corsica, no casualties.

text.p: Four bombs exploded on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica during the night, destroying two cars and damaging local government offices but causing no casualties, police said on Saturday.

No one immediately claimed responsibility for the bombings but such attacks are common on the resort island where separatist groups have waged a campaign for two decades for greater autonomy from mainland France.
The first bomb exploded at 10.15 p.m. on Friday at Biguglia, south of Bastia, destroying a car belonging to an executive at agriculture ministry offices.
A second blast 10 minutes later, just outside Bastia, destroyed another car whose owner was not immediately identified.
The next bombing, 35 minutes later, badly damaged a second agriculture ministry office building and five cars in the town of Pietrabugno.
The final blast of the night, at 2.20 a.m. on Saturday, blew the door off the city hall in Ghisoni, 70 km (45 miles) south of Bastia.

The outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing has stepped up its guerrilla campaign since the detention on December 16 of Francois Santoni, head of the Conculta Naziunalista, the FLNC's legal wing.
Santoni faces charges of attempted extortion and arms violations.
